choices.text: Use the Tuesday nonstop landing at 10:35 a.m., keep the two-night hotel, and revisit only if setup moves before noon or checked gear is added.
Book Monday arrival for every out-of-state kickoff, add a third hotel night, and keep Tuesday morning free regardless of flight buffers.
Treat a Tuesday client start as requiring a prior-night hotel, then request approval for the added Monday night before comparing arrivals.
Skip the nonstop and route through an earlier connection so the hotel stays two nights even if the connection shortens the buffer.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Prior-day arrival is tempting because several earlier work trips used Sunday or prior-evening positioning. Here, however, the required time and protected nonstop make the same-day option a live operational choice rather than a blanket arrival pattern.
probes.gold_action: Use the Tuesday nonstop landing at 10:35 a.m., keep the two-night hotel, and revisit only if setup moves before noon or checked gear is added.
probes.label_rationale: This choice uses the actual first required time, gear status, weather, approval scope, and nonstop buffer. The cited sessions include both resistance to unnecessary extra nights and prior-day arrivals when lab, setup, or schedule facts made same-day travel fragile.
probes.query: Erin is planning Denver to Hartford for a Tuesday client kickoff in West Hartford. The only required activity is a 2:00 p.m. badge and setup window; the nonstop lands Tuesday at 10:35 a.m.; she has no checked demo gear; the forecast is clear; the client described it as a two-night trip. Which planning policy should be applied?

choices.text: Fly Sunday late afternoon, check in near the hospital, collect the checked scanner, and reserve Monday morning for lab access.
Use the Monday first nonstop whenever a city has a nonstop, and count the 40-minute drive as sufficient for the 8:30 lab.
Book Sunday arrival for every Monday hospital project, even where gear and weather would not require it.
Add Saturday for equipment trips so a full nonwork day is available before any lab setup.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choice C reaches a similar itinerary through an overbroad Monday-work rule, while Choice B borrows from same-day examples. The probe is hard because the correct itinerary is a prior-day arrival, but the reason must remain tied to this trip's facts.
probes.gold_action: Fly Sunday late afternoon, check in near the hospital, collect the checked scanner, and reserve Monday morning for lab access.
probes.label_rationale: Sunday arrival is justified by the current lab time, checked scanner, dock timing, winter risk, and approved hotel night. The cited sessions show that prior-day positioning was selected when those facts mattered, while same-day arrivals were used when the buffer protected the first obligation.
probes.query: Erin is planning Denver to Salt Lake City for a Monday 8:30 a.m. hospital lab. A demo scanner must travel as checked equipment; the receiving dock opens only after check-in; canyon snow showers are possible; Sunday hotel approval is already granted. The first same-day nonstop lands Monday at 7:20 a.m. with a 40-minute drive. Which planning policy should be applied?

choices.text: Use the Monday nonstop landing at 10:55 a.m., keep the hotel Monday-Wednesday, and add Sunday only if AV moves into Monday morning.
Book Sunday afternoon arrival and a Sunday hotel because optional welcome events should be treated as work obligations.
Book Sunday arrival for any Monday rollout so Monday morning is never used for flight recovery.
Choose a cheaper Monday connection landing near 1:30 p.m. because the 2:30 AV check still leaves a nominal buffer.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choices B and C are attractive because Sunday arrivals often appeared before Monday work. Choice D is also plausible on cost, leaving more than one defensible plan while still requiring the policy to follow the present agenda rather than a repeated pattern.
probes.gold_action: Use the Monday nonstop landing at 10:55 a.m., keep the hotel Monday-Wednesday, and add Sunday only if AV moves into Monday morning.
probes.label_rationale: The operative facts are a noon-plus required start, carry-on travel, a nonstop with usable buffer, ordinary weather, and no required Sunday event. The cited sessions support adding a prior night only when setup, calibration, lab access, or timing risk makes same-day travel brittle.
probes.query: Erin has a Denver to Atlanta rollout. There is an optional Sunday welcome drink, but the first required item is a Monday 2:30 p.m. AV check at the Midtown hotel; she is carry-on only; a nonstop lands Monday at 10:55 a.m.; weather is normal; an extra Sunday hotel needs a manager note. Which planning policy should be applied?

choices.text: Use airport rideshare or Logan Express, walk the connected conference path, and take short rideshares for dinners.
Reserve a compact SUV for the full conference to preserve independent ground transport on Erin's work trips.
Book an airport rental for every conference and treat rideshares as backup after parking is checked.
Rent a midsize SUV whenever business travel includes evening networking away from the hotel.

probes.difficulty_rationale: The rental choices are tempting because prior clinic loops and equipment trips did use cars and SUVs. The Boston facts make walking, shuttle, and short rides operationally strong enough that a full-stay rental should not be treated as Erin's usual pattern.
probes.gold_action: Use airport rideshare or Logan Express, walk the connected conference path, and take short rideshares for dinners.
probes.label_rationale: The current trip is urban, conference-centered, gear-light, and parking-heavy, matching no-rental decisions in the cited sessions. Rentals and SUVs were used when sites were suburban, spread out, or gear-heavy, not as a standing transport mode.
probes.query: Erin is attending a Boston medical conference based at the Hynes Convention Center. Her hotel connects by indoor walkway; the days are sessions and networking in Back Bay; she has a laptop and carry-on only; Logan Express or airport rideshare works; hotel parking is $58 per night. Which ground-transport policy should be applied?

choices.text: Reserve a compact SUV at CLE, use suburban hotels with free parking, and return the SUV before the flight home.
Use rideshares and couriers between all sites because city-area business trips should stay rental-free.
Reserve a standard SUV for every work trip with presentations, even if sites are walkable.
Skip a rental until a personal day trip is added, then handle clinic transfers by app rides.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choices B and D sound plausible because Erin has rejected rentals in several conference cities. Choice C echoes SUV-heavy trips. The correct plan must recognize that this fresh itinerary has the site geography and equipment load that make a rental practical.
probes.gold_action: Reserve a compact SUV at CLE, use suburban hotels with free parking, and return the SUV before the flight home.
probes.label_rationale: The compact SUV is supported by this loop's spread-out suburbs, cartons, rolling case, and free parking. The cited sessions show cars and SUVs for multi-site or gear-heavy trips, while rental-free plans fit conference-centered urban trips.
probes.query: Erin is building a Cleveland/Akron clinic loop: Monday delivery in Beachwood, Tuesday training in Akron, Wednesday demo in Westlake, two cartons plus a rolling case, suburban hotels with free parking, and no useful transit between sites. Which ground-transport policy should be applied?

choices.text: Use BART, walking, and rideshares for the summit, adding a one-day rental only if Napa becomes firm.
Reserve a compact SUV for the whole stay because Erin typically wants control of ground transport.
Pick up a rental at SFO for every summit to keep offsite meetings and dinners flexible.
Rent a standard SUV whenever any Bay Area offsite appears, even if the site is transit-accessible.

probes.difficulty_rationale: The offsite meeting and possible Napa trip make a car seem defensible, while previous SUV trips make Choices B and D tempting. The key distinction is that the driving extension is not firm and the core agenda works without a rental.
probes.gold_action: Use BART, walking, and rideshares for the summit, adding a one-day rental only if Napa becomes firm.
probes.label_rationale: The summit is urban, parking is expensive, gear is light, and the offsite is transit-accessible, so full-stay rental value is low. The cited sessions separate rental-free urban conferences from SUV or rental choices tied to suburban sites, gear, or confirmed driving extensions.
probes.query: Erin is in San Francisco for a downtown policy summit. Sessions are at Moscone; one reception is in SoMa; the only offsite meeting is near Oakland City Center and can be reached by BART or rideshare; she has no demo gear; hotel parking is $64 per night; a Napa day trip is only a maybe. Which ground-transport policy should be applied?

choices.text: Book the Brandon-area business hotel for work nights, prioritizing the short load-in and 7:45 setup over the waterfront pool.
Choose the closest practical hotel for every training week, even when later agendas favor a more experiential area.
Choose the downtown waterfront hotel whenever ratings and pool amenities are stronger, and drive in early.
Book the downtown scene for all trips with evenings free, even when the morning commute is longer.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choice B reaches the same hotel outcome through an overbroad training-week rule, and Choices C and D are plausible because Erin has chosen experiential locations on other trips. The probe tests whether the worksite choice is tied to the present setup burden.
probes.gold_action: Book the Brandon-area business hotel for work nights, prioritizing the short load-in and 7:45 setup over the waterfront pool.
probes.label_rationale: For this trip, early setup, equipment handling, and short load-in outweigh the waterfront amenity gap. The cited sessions show commute-focused hotel choices for tight work mornings or equipment, but also resort and weekend-oriented choices when the room or setting was central.
probes.query: Erin is choosing lodging for a Tampa training. Required setup is 7:45 a.m. at a Brandon clinic on Tuesday and Wednesday; two demo boxes must be loaded; parking is free. A plain business hotel is 8 minutes away, while a higher-rated downtown waterfront property with a pool is 35 to 45 minutes away in rush hour. Which hotel policy should be applied?

choices.text: Book the Rittenhouse hotel for the full stay, accepting the longer walk because sessions start late and the weekend room matters.
Book the closest convention hotel for every work trip, then add rides only if a commute becomes impossible.
Demote any hotel beyond a few minutes from the worksite, even when a spouse weekend is attached.
Choose a leisure-feel hotel for every trip with after-hours free time, regardless of workday timing.

probes.difficulty_rationale: The closest convention hotel remains defensible because work sessions are part of the trip, making Choices B and C tempting. Choice D overgeneralizes leisure-oriented selections, so the correct plan must balance this particular agenda rather than use a fixed location rule.
probes.gold_action: Book the Rittenhouse hotel for the full stay, accepting the longer walk because sessions start late and the weekend room matters.
probes.label_rationale: The later starts, light gear, and spouse weekend shift the location trade-off toward the better room and evening setting. The cited sessions show that closer hotels were chosen for tight work logistics, while resort or weekend districts won when downtime and companions mattered more.
probes.query: Erin has a Philadelphia workshop. Sessions start at 10:30 a.m. at the convention center; she has no equipment beyond a laptop; Mark is joining Friday through Sunday. The Rittenhouse hotel has better rooms and restaurants and is an 18-minute walk, while the closest convention hotel is basic and a 4-minute walk. Which hotel policy should be applied?

choices.text: Book the campus hotel, send the kits there, and use the shorter Monday move despite the smaller room.
Book the closest worksite hotel for every client trip, regardless of amenities or later leisure plans.
Choose the nicer harbor hotel whenever room quality is higher, and drive in early with the kits.
Use an experiential waterfront base for all campus trips because evenings outweigh commute savings.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choice B is tempting because it produces the same booking through a broad closest-hotel pattern. Choices C and D borrow from amenity and waterfront examples. The distinction is that the current kit handling and early setup create the commute priority.
probes.gold_action: Book the campus hotel, send the kits there, and use the shorter Monday move despite the smaller room.
probes.label_rationale: The campus hotel is selected because it can receive the kits and protects a 7:15 a.m. setup. The cited sessions support proximity when equipment and first-morning risk dominate, while also showing non-close choices for recovery weekends and spouse-oriented stays.
probes.query: Erin is planning New Haven campus training. Calibration kits are being shipped to the hotel; first setup is Monday at 7:15 a.m.; the closest campus hotel can receive boxes but has smaller rooms. A harbor hotel is nicer and 25 minutes away with morning traffic. Which hotel policy should be applied?

choices.text: Book the attached block Monday-Thursday for forum work, then price a separate Friday independent stay if friends commit.
Book the independent suite for all nights because conference blocks should lose to lower rates and larger rooms.
Book the official block for the entire trip whenever a conference offers one, including any Friday social night.
Avoid the block whenever a personal night is possible, and keep one independent hotel for all nights.

probes.difficulty_rationale: The cheaper suite and possible Friday plan make independent lodging defensible, while earlier trips include both block use and independent stays. Choices B, C, and D each turn one recurring pattern into a one-size conference policy.
probes.gold_action: Book the attached block Monday-Thursday for forum work, then price a separate Friday independent stay if friends commit.
probes.label_rationale: The attached block materially reduces badge, early-start, teardown, and carton-handling risk for the forum nights, while the possible Friday social stay can be evaluated separately. The cited sessions show block, independent, and split strategies depending on agenda pressure and extension value.
probes.query: Erin is attending an Austin product forum, arriving Monday evening. The official block hotel is attached to the meeting floor at $249; an independent suite is $209 and a 12-minute walk. Badge pickup is 7:15 a.m. Tuesday, booth teardown ends 5:45 p.m. Thursday, and two cartons must be handled. She may stay Friday for friends. Which lodging policy should be applied?

choices.text: Book the independent suite for the whole stay on a cancellable rate, since it is closer to sessions and better for the weekend.
Use the official block for every symposium so registration and hotel folios stay together.
Avoid all official blocks on principle and book independent lodging before comparing agenda risk.
Split between the block and independent hotel on all spouse trips, even when the block is farther.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choice C lands on a similar booking but for the wrong broad reason, while Choice B echoes successful block choices elsewhere. The context leaves both block and independent defensible until shuttle time, fees, agenda pressure, and weekend plans are weighed.
probes.gold_action: Book the independent suite for the whole stay on a cancellable rate, since it is closer to sessions and better for the weekend.
probes.label_rationale: The independent suite wins on current facts: it is closer after the shuttle comparison, cheaper after fees, cancellable, and better for the spouse extension, with no early booth or teardown risk. The cited sessions show independent choices when value and extension fit were stronger, and block choices when event logistics mattered.
probes.query: Erin is planning a Las Vegas symposium Monday through Thursday with a Saturday spouse extension. The official resort block has a high fee and a 25-minute shuttle to the meeting hall; a cancellable independent non-casino suite is across the street from sessions and cheaper after fees. First session is 10:00 a.m.; there is no booth or teardown. Which lodging policy should be applied?

choices.text: Use the connected block Monday-Thursday nights, then move to Fells Point Friday-Saturday for the leisure portion.
Stay in the official block every night of any conference, even when weekend plans favor another area.
Book Fells Point for all nights whenever a leisure extension is attached, accepting daily rideshares to sessions.
Avoid changing hotels at conferences and choose one independent property for the whole stay.

probes.difficulty_rationale: One-hotel simplicity and the leisure extension make Choices C and D plausible, while prior block wins make Choice B tempting. The correct policy is not a fixed block or independent stance; it follows the work-versus-weekend split in this itinerary.
probes.gold_action: Use the connected block Monday-Thursday nights, then move to Fells Point Friday-Saturday for the leisure portion.
probes.label_rationale: The split plan uses the block where early breakfasts and late receptions make connected access valuable, then switches when leisure setting becomes the main purpose. The cited sessions include partial-block, independent-full-stay, and work-block-plus-weekend strategies driven by the agenda.
probes.query: Erin has a Baltimore analytics congress, arriving Monday. The official block is connected to Tuesday-Thursday sessions and includes 7:00 a.m. breakfasts plus late receptions. A Fells Point hotel is better for Friday-Saturday leisure but requires a 15-minute rideshare to the congress. Cancellation terms are similar. Which lodging policy should be applied?

choices.text: Take the Thursday 7:10 p.m. nonstop home, using the afternoon buffer and keeping Friday morning clear.
After Thursday client work, add Thursday night and fly Friday morning as the standard calmer pattern.
Avoid evening returns after workshops, even when the airport buffer is over three hours.
Book Friday morning for all trips with Thursday end times so checkout and airport math are avoided.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Friday morning sounds appealing because several later work trips were extended. The challenge is that those extensions came from concrete risks absent here, while this itinerary resembles successful same-day evening returns.
probes.gold_action: Take the Thursday 7:10 p.m. nonstop home, using the afternoon buffer and keeping Friday morning clear.
probes.label_rationale: The ending time, short airport transfer, lack of checked gear, no rental return, and Friday commitments make same-day return reliable. The cited sessions show same-day returns when buffers held and next-morning returns when teardown, gear, weather, or transfer math made the evening flight fragile.
probes.query: Erin's Charlotte client workshop ends Thursday at 2:30 p.m. The airport is 25 minutes away; there is no checked equipment; no rental car is involved; a 7:10 p.m. nonstop to Denver is available. Friday morning has internal calls. Which return policy should be applied?

choices.text: Add Thursday night and take the Friday 9:20 a.m. nonstop, avoiding the late demo, checked case, rental return, and weather squeeze.
Take a Thursday evening flight whenever one exists, keeping extra hotel nights out of work trips.
Use Friday morning after every Thursday demo, regardless of end time, gear, weather, or airport distance.
Set a hard stop on every Thursday demo so Erin can keep an evening return instead of adding a hotel night.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choice C reaches the same day-of-return outcome through a broad Thursday-demo pattern, while Choices B and D overapply same-day return discipline. Multiple choices sound operational, but only one ties the extra night to the actual risk stack.
probes.gold_action: Add Thursday night and take the Friday 9:20 a.m. nonstop, avoiding the late demo, checked case, rental return, and weather squeeze.
probes.label_rationale: The next-morning return is justified by the current late end, checked case, rental return, long drive, weather risk, and approved hotel night. The cited sessions show next-day returns under similar transfer pressure, alongside same-day returns when the final-day buffer was reliable.
probes.query: Erin's Omaha/Council Bluffs demo day now runs until 5:15 p.m. Thursday. She has a checked demo case, a rental return, a 45-minute airport drive, a winter advisory, and an approved hotel night. A Friday 9:20 a.m. nonstop is available. Which return policy should be applied?

choices.text: Use the 10:30 p.m. Thursday nonstop after dinner, with bag storage confirmed and no Friday hotel.
Add Thursday night and fly Friday morning whenever a summit includes an evening dinner.
Avoid late-night same-day flights after conferences, even when they preserve Friday commitments.
Leave before the sponsor dinner on an earlier flight because work trips should end as soon as sessions close.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Choices B and C are tempting because many trips added the extra night after late workdays. Choice D is plausible for schedule simplicity. The correct plan must recognize that a late flight can be the cleaner current-trip solution rather than treating Friday morning as the routine answer.
probes.gold_action: Use the 10:30 p.m. Thursday nonstop after dinner, with bag storage confirmed and no Friday hotel.
probes.label_rationale: The late same-day return works because bag storage is available, there is no gear or rental return, the dinner has value, and Friday has a competing commitment. The cited sessions show Erin using late same-day options when buffers and current-trip objectives supported them, and moving to next morning only when final-day logistics became fragile.
probes.query: Erin's Los Angeles summit ends Thursday at 4:00 p.m. The hotel can store bags; she has no demo equipment; no rental car is involved; a useful sponsor dinner ends by 8:15 p.m. A 10:30 p.m. nonstop from LAX is available, and Friday has a family appointment.
